subject: vintage

cdp-2021.name: Châteauneuf-du-Pape growers' syndicate, 2021 vintage page
cdp-2021.note: Written before the harvest was fully in, so yield and alcohol are early estimates.

european-cellars.name: European Cellars, Châteauneuf-du-Pape, the vintage game
european-cellars.note: Importer for Rhône estates. Quotes growers, including Domaine Roger Sabon.

wine-spectator.name: Wine Spectator, Southern Rhône vintage chart
wine-spectator.note: Region-wide score and a short note. Excerpts only.

claims.claim: Winter was unusually mild, about 2.5°C above average in February. Spring was very cool.

A cold night on 7 to 8 April threatened the early buds (Grenache, Syrah, Bourboulenc). Châteauneuf was largely spared, helped by wind and the Rhône nearby. Edge-of-vineyard lows were about -1.5°C, against -7°C elsewhere in the Vaucluse.
claims.note: The syndicate has reason to play down damage. Wine Spectator says frosts cut yields in the south.

claims.claim: Summer had a few short, very hot spells (mid-June, end of July, mid-August). Rain of 55 to 77 mm, with early-August showers, kept the vines from serious water stress.
claims.note: One source. European Cellars calls the season cool and rainy, barely tempered by short heat spikes.

claims.claim: It was a late vintage with a long season. Vines were healthy in early September, with little mildew or oidium. Autumn equinox storms slowed picking, and the last plots came in around early October.

The crop was small. The syndicate expected 20 to 25% below average, about 92,000 hl, with a big gap between frosted and unfrosted parcels. European Cellars says cuts of 25 to 45% and the smallest crop in many years.
claims.note: Both agree on a small crop. Numbers differ. See conflicts.

claims.claim: Reds run lower in alcohol than recent years, around 14 to 14.5%. The syndicate says about 14% in the juices. Domaine Roger Sabon says around 14.5%.
claims.note: Early figures from the syndicate and one grower.

claims.claim: Reds are fresh and lively, with intense colour and good acidity. The syndicate calls it an old-style vintage with beautiful ageing potential, and says the wines can also be enjoyed young. Grenache rewards decanting or a few years in bottle.
claims.quote: An old-style vintage with beautiful aging potential

claims.claim: European Cellars calls 2021 an exceptional vintage for whites and Mourvèdre. The syndicate page does not describe the whites.
claims.note: One importer's view. No critic on the whites was read.

claims.claim: Wine Spectator scores the Southern Rhône 88 for 2021, the lowest of 2018 to 2022, and notes frosts cut yields. Its drink window is drink or hold.
claims.note: A region-wide score. The syndicate and European Cellars are warmer, and European Cellars says growers favour such vintages more than critics.

conflicts: Yield loss: the syndicate expected 20 to 25% below average. European Cellars says 25 to 45% down. Wine Spectator blames frost. The syndicate says frost mostly spared the appellation.

Season: the syndicate describes short, very hot spells and some summer rain. European Cellars calls it a cool, rainy growing season with a few short heat spikes. Both agree it was not a hot year overall.
Quality: Wine Spectator gives 88. European Cellars and the syndicate speak of freshness and ageing potential, and of exceptional whites and Mourvèdre.
gaps: No second independent weather source on the 7 to 8 April cold night.
No critic's report on the whites.
Vinous, Decanter and Wine Advocate 2021 reports not read.
Little on Southern Rhône outside Châteauneuf.

sheet.vintage: A cool, late year. A cold night in April and a cool, damp season cut the crop to one of the smallest in years. The reds are fresh and lively, around 14 to 14.5%, with good acidity and a classic, old-style feel.
sheet.vintage_white: A cool year with a smaller crop, which suits whites. They kept fresh acidity.
